lineup:C:4035538:w1.title: Montgomery outplayed the guy who started
lineup:C:4035538:w1.text: Back in Week 1 you started James Cook III at running back while David Montgomery had the better day parked on your bench. Cook got the start. Montgomery got the receipts.

pos:K1:FLEX6.title: Kicker's elite. Flex is the problem child.
pos:K1:FLEX6.text: Your kicker leads the league and your flex spot, the wild-card slot, is near the bottom. That's the spot where a waiver pickup would actually move the needle.

proj:under:3040151:4035538.title: Kittle's the exception, not the rule
proj:under:3040151:4035538.text: George Kittle keeps clearing his projection, but the rest of your lineup, Montgomery especially, keeps coming up just short of ESPN's number. It roughly cancels out, but it's not a trend to lean on.

lineup:B:4259545:w1.title: Swift made the flex call look rough
lineup:B:4259545:w1.text: In Week 1 you started Emeka Egbuka at flex while D'Andre Swift had a monster day on your bench. Swift by name, forgotten by lineup.

pos:WR1:K8.title: Receivers are elite. Your kicker is on strike.
pos:WR1:K8.text: Your receivers lead the league and your kicker sits dead last. That's the cheapest fix on the whole roster, straight off the waiver wire.

proj:over:4241389:4360248.title: Lamb is doing the heavy lifting
proj:over:4241389:4360248.text: CeeDee Lamb keeps blowing past his projection, and it's covering for Kyle Pitts Sr., who keeps falling short of his. Ride the one that's working.

lineup:C:4241416:w1.title: Hubbard's bench afternoon still stings
lineup:C:4241416:w1.text: In Week 1 you started Jaylen Waddle at flex and got next to nothing back, while Chuba Hubbard quietly went off on your bench. Bet on the player, not the name recognition.

pos:RB3:QB8.title: Running backs strong, quarterback's taking the week off
pos:RB3:QB8.text: Your running backs rank near the top of the league and your quarterback sits last. Quarterback is where a waiver claim would help the most.

proj:under:4258173:4572680.title: Collins is outrunning the forecast
proj:under:4258173:4572680.text: Nico Collins keeps beating his projection, but the rest of the lineup, Tucker Kraft included, has been running behind ESPN's numbers overall. Collins is carrying more than his share.

lineup:D:4248528:w1.title: Your bench earned a promotion weeks ago
lineup:D:4248528:w1.text: In Week 1 you started Quinshon Judkins at flex while Christian Watson put up a massive day on your bench. Watson's bench residency was just getting started.

pos:TE1:RB7.title: Tight end's thriving, running back isn't
pos:TE1:RB7.text: Your tight end leads the league and your running backs sit near the bottom. Running back is exactly where to go shopping on waivers.

proj:under:4361370:3929630.title: Olave's the one outrunning his projection
proj:under:4361370:3929630.text: Chris Olave keeps clearing his projection. Saquon Barkley is dealing with a hamstring injury and has fallen short of his. Watch his status before leaning on that number again.

lineup:C:4432665:w3.title: Bowers had the game, from your bench
lineup:C:4432665:w3.text: Back in Week 3 you started Dalton Schultz at tight end while Brock Bowers quietly torched everyone from your bench. Tight end is streaky. That was the stream you missed.

pos:QB2:K7.title: Quarterback's great, kicker's an afterthought
pos:QB2:K7.text: Your quarterback spot ranks near the top of the league and your kicker is close to the bottom. Kicker is the cheapest upgrade sitting on the waiver wire.

proj:over:4685472:4596448.title: McMillan's outrunning every forecast
proj:over:4685472:4596448.text: Tetairoa McMillan keeps smashing his projection while Bucky Irving keeps falling short of his. ESPN still hasn't adjusted for either.

lineup:B:5083076:w3.title: Fannin's big game, wasted on the bench
lineup:B:5083076:w3.text: In Week 3 you started Tyler Warren at tight end while Harold Fannin Jr. quietly had the better day behind him. Even an unbeaten record has one blemish.

pos:RB1:WR8.title: Running backs carry, receivers napping
pos:RB1:WR8.text: Your running backs lead the league and your receivers sit dead last. Receiver is where a waiver add would do the most good.

proj:over:4430737:4870795.title: Williams is outrunning ESPN's math
proj:over:4430737:4870795.text: Kyren Williams keeps beating his projection while Makai Lemon keeps coming up short of his. The gap is why the record still looks spotless.

lineup:C:4431299:w4.title: This one wasn't a bench mistake
lineup:C:4431299:w4.text: The optimal-lineup math flagged Rome Odunze over Rashee Rice in Week 4, but Rice left that game early with a hamstring injury. There's no decision to second-guess here, just bad luck.

pos:QB1:RB8.title: Quarterback's elite, running back's underwater
pos:QB1:RB8.text: Your quarterback spot leads the league and your running backs sit dead last. Running back is where a waiver claim would help the most.

proj:under:3918298:4429160.title: Allen's elite, Achane's stuck in the mud
proj:under:3918298:4429160.text: Josh Allen keeps clearing his projection, but De'Von Achane keeps falling well short of his. One MVP-caliber week is covering for a lot of underperformance.

lineup:B:15847:w2.title: Kelce had the game, from your bench
lineup:B:15847:w2.text: In Week 2 you started Dallas Goedert at tight end while Travis Kelce, yes, that Travis Kelce, put up a huge day behind him. Even a future Hall of Famer can't help you from the bench.

pos:WR3:DST8.title: Receivers solid, defense is the drag
pos:WR3:DST8.text: Your receivers rank near the top of the league and your defense sits dead last. Defense is the cheapest, easiest upgrade on the waiver wire.

proj:over:4239993:15847.title: Higgins picking up the slack Kelce left behind
proj:over:4239993:15847.text: Tee Higgins keeps beating his projection while Travis Kelce keeps coming up short of his. Father Time remains undefeated.
